measured_on: 2026-10-23, two CloudLab xl170 nodes (Intel E5-2640v4, ConnectX-4 Lx), Ubuntu 22.04, code 68cf2c1

stridedmem:1024:7.note: From loadgen --calibrate on the server node. Readings below 10 us and the 20 us reading are unreliable; use 99.6 iterations per us. So 170 iterations is about 1.7 us of work and 1700 about 17 us.

effective_capacity.note: Beyond the fake work itself, each request costs about 4 us of runtime, network stack, and thread creation on the server, so capacity is lower than kthreads / mean work.
effective_capacity.w0_8_kthreads_17us: saturates between 350k and 400k req/s (about 21 us per request per core)

noise_band.rule: 3 repeats; a difference counts when the medians differ by more than 5% and the two ranges do not overlap (DESIGN.md section 3)
noise_band.note: Ranges are 1-6% of the median at and below the headline load; above it (w1 at 450k) they widen to 25% or more.

client.note: The client misses about 0.15% of send slots at every load (adherence about 99.85%), so loadgen's 'adherence may be low' warning appears everywhere; it is not saturation. The headline-load rule uses a 99% adherence threshold.

budget.formula: Per generation N >= 1, with P = N + 1 existing policies and N + 2 workloads after the new one: new workload x (P policies with hints + fifo ignore) x 2 repeats, plus the new policy x (N + 2 workloads) x 2 repeats, at 56 s each, plus one rebuild (34 s) and a debug-build smoke run (about 90 s). That is (2N + 4) x 112 s + 126 s.
trimming_when_over_cap: re-measure on the new workload only policies whose status is baseline or accepted
drop the two lightest load levels for workloads older than the current generation
one repeat for policies more than 15% behind the best on that workload
budget.per_8h_slot: about 10 generations, counting roughly 10 minutes of agent time per generation

overhead_finding.summary: The hint-enabled build is about 1% slower than stock Caladan at saturation on w0 (376k vs 380k req/s answered) and about 2 us slower in median latency and 5% in p99 near saturation; identical at light load.
overhead_finding.cause: Not the per-pick counters and not the hints mode: switching both off (runtime_sched_stats 0, --ignore-hints) changes nothing measurable. It is the hint build's general pick mechanism (indirect policy call, gap closing) versus stock's one-line pop.
overhead_finding.consequence: All policies share it, so policy comparisons are fair; experiments keep the counters on.
overhead_finding.evidence: results/gen0/notes.md, addendum; runs w0__fifo__*__{hints r3-r4, hints-nostats r1-r2, stock r3-r4}, code 810cfbf
overhead_finding.open_item: Possible fix: inlined fast path in sched_pop_next when only one thread is queued.

hint_build_overhead.note: The hint machinery outside the policy region (per-packet classifier call, hint fields, policy table) costs about 6% of p99 at 0.8 load and 10-18% near saturation on a single-kind workload; per-pick statistics add a few percent more only near saturation. Reported to the owner in generation 0; not changed, since it lies outside the policy region.
